input.brief: Tedits Studio independent web design in Zambia. Keep existing cloud hero, brand fonts and slate ivory palette. After hero a rotating business line and pinned browser story explains finding confidence and enquiry; then direct collaboration, selected concept work, offer and enquiry.

direction.name: Type and nothing else
direction.idea: The first screen is made only of words, colour and space, good enough that nobody misses a picture there. Pictures arrive later, large and few, as relief from the type. This is the honest answer when a subject has nothing worth photographing: instead of inventing illustrations, set what you have to say as well as it can be set. The typography carries a point of view through scale (one enormous statement, everything else small), through measure (a narrow, bookish column or a full-width line), and through one committed colour.
direction.composition: First screen: the statement, two lines at most, set at 9–14vw and occupying the full width with tight leading, positioned in the upper two-thirds. One supporting sentence at 20–24px sits bottom-left on the same margin and the single action sits bottom-right on the same baseline. No navigation bar; two or three links in a top corner. Sections that follow are typographic set pieces, each different: a list of five to eight capabilities set at 4–6vw one per line; a paragraph at 28–36px in a 28ch column pushed to the right half; a pair of large numerals with a sentence each; a single quotation filling a colour field. Each section uses a different horizontal position (left, right, full) so the page has movement without imagery.
direction.typography: This direction lives or dies on the face and its settings. Display at tight tracking and leading; text sizes few and far apart (for example 15, 22, 34 and the display size). Use real typographic detail: proper quotes, balanced line breaks, hung punctuation where it helps.
direction.colour: Either one saturated ground for the whole page with a single ink, or paper and ink with one section inverted and one in the accent as a full field. Colour does the job images would have done.
direction.imagery: The first screen has no picture. Further down, real pictures of the subject's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs) arrive large and few: a full-bleed photograph between two type sections, a looping clip in one band, an archival image beside a list. Do not add icons, shapes, patterns or abstract graphics to compensate for anything.
direction.richness: Scale contrast and colour mass. A capability list set at 5vw is an image in its own right.
direction.pitfalls: Without pictures, weak copy has nowhere to hide: write real sentences. Vary the set pieces; four sections of big-heading-plus-paragraph is a text document, not a design. Keep all headings within two lines.

hero.name: Name across the middle
hero.blueprint: Paper and ink only; no picture on the first screen. The name runs on one line across the vertical centre, sized to span from the 18px left margin to the 18px right margin (97.5% of the width). Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune its vw size to the letter count, so it never wraps. In a heavy grotesk the letters stand about 280px tall, from about 310px to 590px; nothing touches or overlaps them. The four corners carry everything else on 18px margins. Top-left: one supporting sentence at 18px on two lines, max 36ch, and 16px below it the single action as a solid ink rectangle. Top-right: a menu word or three text links at 15px. Bottom-left, on a baseline 24px above the edge: the city or the kind of work at 16px. Bottom-right on the same baseline: two or three text links at 15px. The ground between the corners and the name, about 230px above and below it, stays empty and is closed on both sides by the corner texts. The name returns in the footer at the same width with ground and ink swapped and a two-line invitation above it, so the page closes like a bracket.
hero.mobile: The name stays on one line across the width inside 16px margins and moves up to 22% of the height. The supporting sentence follows on the left margin at 17px, then the action at full width. The lower half holds the first picture of the work as a 4:5 frame cropped by the bottom edge, so the screen does not end in empty paper. A menu word sits top-right.
hero.headline: The name itself on one line, up to about 12 characters; the 18px sentence in the top-left corner says what it is.

photos.title: Fog and quiet
photos.note: misty, muted, minimal landscapes and empty horizons; calm areas for text

motion.name: Scaling wordmark
motion.description: The giant name responds to the scroll: as the first screen leaves, the wordmark scales down a few percent (or grows from 0.94 to 1 as the footer arrives) on a scroll-linked timeline, so the monument feels heavy. Travel stays under 8%. Static fallback where scroll timelines are unsupported. Recipe: 'Scroll-linked progress' in references/motion.md, animating `scale`.

sections.name: Title, note, facts row
sections.blueprint: First row: a heading of two to four words in a light weight at clamp(44px, 5vw, 76px) sits on the left margin in columns 1–6; a three-line paragraph at 16px, 260px wide, sits in columns 10–12 with its last line on the heading's baseline. Columns 7–9 stay empty. 120px lower, a second row sets three or four facts (a date, a time, a place, a price) as large light text at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), spread across the 12 columns with `justify-content: space-between`. Each fact has a one-line explanation at 14px directly under it in the soft ink, left-aligned to the fact. Facts are separated only by the space between them, so the row reads like the line of times on a printed programme. A photograph may start under the right half of the facts row, 5 columns wide at 4:3. Padding 140px top, 120px bottom.
sections.mobile: Heading at 11vw on the left margin; the note follows directly under it at 16px, full width. The facts become a two-column grid with a 32px row gap, each fact at 26px with its explanation beneath. Any photograph goes last, full width.

sections.name: Call and response column
sections.blueprint: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

sections.name: Two columns, highlighted words
sections.blueprint: The story is set as text far larger than anything else on the page: 110–160 words at clamp(22px, 2.1vw, 32px), tight leading 1.18, in the soft ink, flowing through two columns that fill the full width between 24px margins (`columns: 2; column-gap: 32px`, justified, with hyphenation on). No heading. The name at the start is in full ink. Six or seven single words or short phrases carry a flat highlighter background in three or four palette colours, built with an inline `background-color`, `box-decoration-break: clone` and 0.1em of horizontal padding; they mark the facts a scanning reader wants (a place, a year, a client, a skill). The final short sentence is highlighted entire in the strongest colour and is the link to contact. Padding 120px top and bottom. No image and no portrait.
sections.mobile: One column at 20px, left-aligned and unjustified, leading 1.25, with 18px margins. Keep four or five highlights so no line carries two. The final highlighted sentence sits on its own line with 24px above it and works as a full-width tap target.

sections.name: Quiet ledger, side preview
sections.blueprint: A plain ledger in one column 560px wide whose left edge sits at 22% of the viewport width. A heading of two or three words at 24–28px in medium weight, then 32px of space, then one row per project, 44px tall: the name at 16px in full ink at the left, the kind of work at 14px in the soft ink starting at 55% of the column, and the year right-aligned with tabular figures. Nothing is drawn between rows; the three fixed starts make the columns. Hovering or focusing a row keeps it in full ink, drops the others to the soft ink, and shows that project's image in the empty area right of the column: a 4:3 frame 300px wide, `position: absolute`, its top aligned to the hovered row, 64px from the column's right edge, appearing with a 150ms fade. Holds 6–20 rows; group by year with 28px of extra space.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 52px tall: name at the left, year at the right, kind of work on a second line at 13px. There is no hover preview; instead the first three projects each show a 16:10 image at full column width above their row.

sections.name: The price, very large
sections.blueprint: One plan, no card. Columns 1–4 hold a heading of two to four words at 28–36px and one paragraph at 17px, top-aligned. Columns 6–12 hold the price as a display figure: numerals at clamp(120px, 16vw, 240px), tight tracking, leading 0.85, with the currency sign at half that size raised to the cap line and the period (per month, once) at 18px beside the last numeral on the baseline. One thing from the page overlaps the numerals by 10–15% of their height: the product photograph, the interface fragment or the motif shape, placed over the top-right of the figure. Beneath the figure, on its left edge, four plain lines at 18px state what is included, one per line, without ticks or bullets, then a single rectangular button. The section is at least 80svh tall with the figure vertically centred.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first, full width. The figure follows at 34vw, flush left, with the overlapping object tucked at its top-right corner at a third of the screen wide. Included lines at 17px and a full-width button close the block.

sections.name: One field, nothing else
sections.blueprint: The whole section is one prompt and one field in a column 520px wide, on the page's text column line or centred, with 200px of empty ground above and 160px below. The prompt is two lines at one size, 24–28px in medium weight: the first line in the soft ink, the second in full ink. 28px below, a single input 520px wide and 64px tall with a 12px radius, filled with the lightest tone on the page so it is the only bright surface in view; no outline at rest and a 2px inner ring in the accent on focus. Inside the right end of the field, 8px from its edge, a round submit button 44px across with an arrow and an accessible name. 16px below the field, one line at 13px says what happens next. 72px lower, three label and value rows at 14px: email, phone, address.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Prompt at 22px. The field stays one row, 60px tall, with the arrow button inside its right end. The three label and value rows stack with the label above each value and 20px between them.

references.name: CoffeeTech®
references.idea: Present an industrial roaster maker like a design brand: one enormous three-word statement on black, with the machine withheld until the first scroll, where it emerges from the dark.
references.hero: Near-black viewport with nothing but type. A centred three-line headline, one word per line, in Inter Medium at about 15vw with tight tracking; the first line starts a third of the way down and the last runs to within 35px of the bottom edge, its widest word spanning roughly 70% of the width. Cream letters; no subhead, no media, no hero button. Navigation is one quiet row: logo with a terracotta mark at left, four text links centred, then a filled terracotta 'Products' button with a grid icon, an outlined contact button and a language dropdown at right. The top third stays empty.
references.type: Inter throughout at weight 500. Display lines at 216px with -0.07em tracking and leading near 0.95 against 14px body, a jump of about 15 times. Secondary headlines near 10vw, intro paragraph around 26px. Section labels are tiny and wrapped in square brackets.
references.colour: #0d0e13 #e5e2dd #f3ece2 #c8603d #262629 — Blue-black and warm putty-grey sections alternate; cream type on dark, near-black on light. Terracotta appears only on the logo mark and the primary button.
references.imagery: Studio shots of roasters: a black machine barely lit against black after the hero, then white and black machines as cut-outs on pale-grey tiles. One warm founder portrait with a signature overlapping its edge; macro bean photos in small-radius cards.
references.layout: Outer margins of about 70px. A centred type poster on top, then an offset two-column intro, then a product grid pushed into the right two-thirds with its bracketed label alone in the left third. Oversized left-flush headlines open and close the lower page.

sections.description: Warm putty-grey band entered through a hairline. A portrait about 290px wide with 8px corners sits in the left third; a scrawled signature overlaps its bottom-right corner and spills onto the background. A seven-line paragraph at about 26px, medium weight, roughly 510px wide, begins at the horizontal midpoint, followed by a small underlined text link. No heading; the right quarter and the gap between the two elements stay empty.

A headline at roughly 10vw is flush to the left edge and clipped by the right, like a slow marquee. Below, a tiny bracketed label sits alone in the left third; the right two-thirds hold a two-column grid of pale-grey tiles about 400px wide with a small radius, each with a centred machine cut-out, the model name beneath and a tiny outlined pill for its category. The grid closes with a 64px underlined 'see all' text link with an arrow.

Back to blue-black. A cream contact headline at about 10vw sits hard against the left edge, far larger than anything near it. Underneath, the terracotta logo mark is enlarged to about 140px at left; four narrow link columns in small grey text run from 28% to 85% of the width; a pill-shaped back-to-top button sits at far right, with a thin legal row at the bottom.

steal: Let a three-word headline at about 15vw be the entire first viewport and withhold the product until the first scroll.
Photograph a dark product on a background matching the page colour so it appears to emerge from the page rather than sit in a box.
Overlap a handwritten signature onto the corner of a portrait so an about block feels signed rather than laid out.
references.media: The fold is type only; one scroll later a full-bleed low-key photograph of the roaster on matching black covers 76% of the screen, so the object floats out of the dark as the second beat of the hero. Below: a portrait with a signature over its edge, product renders contained on tinted tiles in a 2x2 grid, three 4:5 macro ingredient cards with the label docked bottom-left, and a blog slider; 25 images, no video, about 12.5px corners on card media.
references.motion: No entrance at all: the 400ms frame already matches the settled one. No smooth scroll, pins or sticky elements; a model scale-in keyframe over 1.2s cubic-bezier(.36,.18,0,.99) with a 1.5s glow grows the roaster into place, link underlines wipe in by clip-path over 2.5s, overlay panels slide in over 0.8s, and the most common duration is 0.3s.

references.name: Spatial
references.idea: Typography behaves like sound in a room: plain black statements swell, stretch and bend through an empty white viewport as you scroll.
references.hero: A white viewport holding only the festival dates: two centred lines in Neue Haas Grotesk Roman at roughly 6.7vw, black, tight leading, sitting at the exact vertical middle and spanning about half the width. Large empty fields above and below; no image, no button, no supporting copy. The header is the only other element: a light uppercase wordmark with tight tracking flush to the top-left corner at a 20px inset, and nine small bold uppercase links in a row across the top right. Mobile is the same poster at 40px with a two-line hamburger.
references.type: One face, Neue Haas Grotesk Display 55 Roman, for everything: statements from 56px up to about 10vw, 13px body, bold 13px uppercase navigation, a timetable at about 16px with tight leading. Statement lines are distorted per glyph, each letter scaled to a different width and height.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e8a25c — Pure black on pure white; the programme section inverts to white on black. The only colour is the amber haze of a single photograph.
references.imagery: Almost none. The images are canvas-rendered text statements warped and magnified until letter fragments become abstract black shapes cropped by the viewport. One warm, hazy venue photograph sits inset at half width beside body copy, square-cornered.
references.layout: Full width with 10 to 20px margins. Opens with one centred statement per screen, then drops into left-aligned two-column copy and, further down, edge-to-edge four-column timetables. The swing between empty poster screens and tightly packed listings is the page's rhythm.

sections.description: A run of full-viewport white screens, each carrying one centred two-line sentence. The text is drawn on canvas and deformed: letters within a word have different widths and heights and baselines wobble. Between screens the type is magnified so far that only the strokes and counters of a few letters cross the frame, cropped on every side, while a small readable version of the next sentence appears inside the wreckage of the previous one.

A calm reset: a three-line centred statement at about 5vw in undistorted type fills the top half. At the bottom, a column of 16px body copy about 650px wide sits flush to the left margin, and an amber-toned photograph starts at the horizontal centre and runs to the right margin with square corners, cropped by the fold.

Black full-bleed section. Day headings are single small lines above a hairline; under each, a four-column table spans the full width: artist flush left, format at one third, room at two thirds, time range right-aligned at the far edge. Rows are about 35px high with a hairline between each, all in the same 30px grotesk with no bold; changeovers are marked by rows in capitals.

steal: Open with a single factual line (the dates) centred on an otherwise empty white screen instead of a branded hero.
Scale each letter of a statement independently in width and height so plain grotesk type looks as if it is resonating.
Set a programme as a full-width four-column hairline table in one size and weight, times right-aligned, on an inverted background.

references.name: Nodeck
references.idea: A consultancy that claims to sell thinking rather than slides builds its site as a slide deck anyway, complete with prev/next buttons, a slide counter and presenter notes.
references.hero: Flat bubblegum-pink viewport. Centre: the name as a sticker, white ultra-heavy caps with a thick black outline and offset black extrusion, bent along a gentle arc and slightly rotated, about 72% wide and 30% tall. A two-word caps label sits 80px above it; a two-line caps tagline at ~1.1vw sits below, two of its words swiped in fluorescent yellow. Photographic props crop off the corners: a yellow sticky note top-left and a highlighter pen entering top-right whose tip touches the last letter. Bottom edge is deck chrome: notes link left; previous, round lime menu and next buttons with hard black offset shadows centred; mute icon and slide counter right.
references.type: The wordmark is an SVG sticker in ultra-black caps. Slide titles use BN Dime Display, a fat irregular display sans, uppercase at ~7vw. Everything else is DM Sans uppercase at 14 to 16px regular. Two sizes, a sevenfold jump.
references.colour: #ff87ab #f5e4d6 #000000 #ffffff #def915 #e9d68b — Each slide is a flat field, pink then cream, with black type; fluorescent lime-yellow is the action and highlight colour (menu button, highlighter swipes, transition wipes). Warm and saturated.
references.imagery: Top-down cut-out photos of desk stationery (sticky note, highlighter, pink eraser) with soft shadows, cropped by the viewport corners and positioned to touch the type. Otherwise type only.
references.layout: One fixed full-viewport stage per slide rather than a scrolling page: a centred title or statement in the middle, a small logo sticker pinned top-centre after slide one, and a persistent control bar along the bottom edge. Ten slides.

sections.description: Every slide opens on a cream full-viewport title card carrying only a tiny caps slide-number label and, about 20px beneath it, the slide's title in fat black display caps at ~7vw, centred slightly above the middle. The title rises from behind a mask, then gives way to the slide body on the same stage. A fluorescent yellow brush-stroke band wipes across the screen between slides.

A pink stage with the small sticker logo pinned top-centre and a pink eraser photograph cropped near the top-right corner. A tiny caps slide label sits at one third height; body copy then builds in word by word in heavy caps starting from the left margin at mid-height. The deck controls stay fixed along the bottom edge throughout, with the counter advancing.

steal: Borrow another medium's chrome (deck controls, slide counter, presenter notes) as the site's navigation to make the brand's argument.
Crop real desk objects off the viewport corners and let one physically touch the wordmark so photo and type share a scene.
Use a highlighter swipe both as text emphasis and as the full-screen transition wipe, tying a small detail to the large motion.
